title: Quine ranks compounds that shift pancreatic cancer cells toward a basal state
summary: Microsoft's Quine, a multimodal biology world model, prioritized thousands of compounds for shifting tumor cell states, and a handful were tested in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines. The top-ranked compounds produced the largest classical-to-basal shifts, as validated by wet-lab experiments, and some moved cells toward a distinct third phenotype. The post gives no quantitative wet-lab figures and links no paper, and it measures cell-state changes rather than clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Quine, multimodal biology world model with interactive harness
organization: Microsoft Research; Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT

evidence.tested: A handful of top-ranked compounds predicted by Quine were tested in patient-derived pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines, where the largest classical-to-basal transcriptional shifts were reported.
evidence.unknown: The page calls the drug-repurposing findings early evidence and does not report how many compounds were tested or the assay statistics.
evidence.ai_role: Quine, a multimodal biology world model with a harness, ranked thousands of compounds by their predicted ability to shift tumor cell states.
